title: The Machines that Make the Machines | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA's Seattle Robotics Lab reports its attempt to automate GB300 tester-tray assembly with Foxconn-set targets of 99.5% success and under 2x human cycle time: a classical modular stack hit over 95% on busbar assembly (160s vs 124s target), while connector insertion reached 90-95% by combining a specialist pose estimator (DOPER), 3D-printed fingers and sim-to-real plus real-world RL. The lessons: classical methods, mechanical design and real-world data still beat pure end-to-end learning where data is scarce.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's Seattle Robotics Lab and Isaac team targeted GB300 tester-tray assembly, chiefly busbar assembly (16 screw locations) and multi-connector insertion, which it calls one of the hardest problems tackled in its nine years, an instance of Moravec's paradox.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Assembly of AI servers is a hard, high-value automation target where dexterity, not compute, is the limit.
insights.quote: Enabling robots to assemble GB300 trays is one of the hardest problems SRL has tackled in nine years
insights.locator: Problems at hand: Moravec returns

insights.claim: Rapid design cycles and low volumes make fixed automation infeasible for GB300 trays, so robots must be flexible and adaptive to part uncertainty, which NVIDIA calls a strategic priority.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Short product cycles in AI hardware favour adaptive robotics over fixtures-based automation.
insights.locator: In GB300 tester-tray assembly, uncertainty must be addressed

insights.claim: Manufacturers asked for 99.5% success and cycle times of no more than twice skilled workers (124 seconds for busbar, 72 seconds for four connectors) with no unintended collisions, a bar far above the 50-90% success rates academic robotics often treats as solved.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Industrial acceptance thresholds are much stricter than research benchmarks, widening the lab-to-factory gap.
insights.quote: In robotics research, 50%-60% success rates are often sufficient, and 80%-90% success rates can be enough to call a task solved.
insights.locator: The second key challenge is performance

insights.claim: Robotics research under-weights statistical rigor, running 10 to 20 trials per task, while verifying 99.5% success with a one-sided 95% confidence bound requires zero failures across at least 598 trials, potentially hundreds of duplicate components.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Proving industrial reliability is itself a costly data problem for learning-based robots.
insights.quote: zero failures must be observed over at least 598 trials
insights.locator: In addition, even if the system is robust or adaptive enough

insights.claim: NVIDIA's strategy was 'the right tool at the right time': try classical baselines first, then imitation learning, sim-to-real RL, real-world RL and VLAs only where they fall short, in contrast to a research culture that rewards novelty over strong baselines.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Disciplined baselining avoids unnecessary complexity in production robotics.
insights.locator: Technical strategy: The right tool at the right time

insights.claim: A classical modular pipeline (FoundationPose perception, waypoint planning with Lissajous-curve primitives, impedance control) was so effective for busbar assembly that no pivot to end-to-end learning was needed, and it was easier to debug and distribute across arms.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Modular classical stacks remain competitive with learned policies for structured industrial tasks.
insights.quote: As it turns out, the classical pipeline was highly effective, and no pivot was needed.
insights.locator: Assembling a busbar: Revisiting the classics

insights.claim: Busbar assembly used three arms (two Flexiv Rizon 4S and a UR10e with an OnRobot screwdriver) and reached over 95% success, with failures mostly from grasp errors and slippage, and a 160-second cycle versus the 124-second target because sequential screwdriving is the bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Busbar automation is near requirements, with a clear path to cut cycle time by parallelising screwing.
insights.locator: Our busbar assembly solution achieved success rates above 95%

themes.theme: Connector insertion: the inverse bitter lesson

insights.claim: Generalist pose estimation failed on small, textureless connectors and behavior cloning with ACT or diffusion policies failed because few specialised cables existed and each deformed after limited use, which NVIDIA calls an 'inverse bitter lesson' where scale is intractable.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: In data-scarce physical settings, domain-knowledge methods can beat scale-based approaches.
insights.quote: scale can be intractable due to physical, financial, and logistical phenomena
insights.locator: Multi-connector insertion: ‘Inverse bitter lesson’

insights.claim: SAM3 segmentation with a fitted centerline and a midpoint grasp lifted cables with almost no observed failures.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Simple off-the-shelf segmentation can solve sub-problems that look hard.
insights.quote: This simple approach produced almost no observed failures.
insights.locator: We began by again implementing a classical pipeline

insights.claim: DOPER (Deep Object Pose Estimation Revisited) trains a lightweight CNN on synthetic CAD renderings, then fine-tunes with pseudolabels from a neural reconstruction of the real part, running at 30 Hz or faster, which let one arm reorient a connector for a second arm to grasp.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Part-specific synthetic-plus-real pose estimators are a practical path for textureless industrial parts.
insights.locator: We returned to pose estimation

insights.claim: Sim-to-real RL in Isaac Lab worked for the large connector but not the small one because tiny pose-estimation errors made it slip, so NVIDIA added SPARR, a real-world residual policy using force-torque inputs on top of a simulation-trained base policy.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Real-world residual learning closes the sim-to-real gap where simulation alone is insufficient.
insights.quote: there is no substitute for real-world data
insights.locator: Sim-to-real transfer achieved high success rates for the large connector

insights.claim: The integrated multi-connector system achieved 90-95% success with a 40-second average per cable, short of deployment requirements, with failures from multi-arm coordination during grasping and delays from slow discrete pose adjustment.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Even the best current result is below the 99.5% bar, so factory deployment is not yet imminent.
insights.locator: Our final multi-connector insertion solution integrated

insights.claim: 3D-printed multi-purpose gripper fingers that constrain part motion during contact made grasp poses far more repeatable without tactile sensors, regrasping or in-hand manipulation, and can be reproduced on a hobby-level 3D printer.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Cheap mechanical design can substitute for sensing and learning complexity.
insights.quote: The finger geometry constrained part motion during contact, making grasp poses far more repeatable.
insights.locator: Interlude 2: Mechanical design as uncertainty reduction

insights.claim: High-performance control with automatic damping design and inertial compensation is underused in robot learning, where most papers use the simplest control laws, yet it improves success and cycle time of RL-learned behaviors.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Control engineering offers untapped performance gains for learning-based robotics.
insights.locator: High-performance control shouldn’t be overlooked

insights.claim: NVIDIA packages libraries as containerized FastAPI robotics services (cuRobo, FoundationPose, FoundationStereo) and uses TALOS, a ros2_control-based orchestration layer running controllers faster than 500 Hz across Franka FR3, Flexiv Rizon 4S, UR10e and SO-101 robots.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Reusable infrastructure is a hidden productivity driver; NVIDIA plans to open-source TALOS and DOPER.
insights.locator: Interlude 1: The unreasonable effectiveness of infrastructure

insights.claim: Cycle time deserves equal priority with success rate, since robot-learning systems mix 1 kHz proprioception, 100 Hz policies, 30 Hz cameras and 5 Hz gripper control, and speed-ups must preserve accuracy and safety.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Throughput, not just accuracy, determines whether learned robots are economically viable.
insights.locator: Cycle time is a worthy counterpart to success rate

themes.theme: Deployment and the path to generalization

insights.claim: Deployment risks include domain mismatch between lab and factory and product design changes; NVIDIA proposes an autonomous-vehicle-style approach of deploying imperfect systems under human supervision and recording interventions to improve continuously.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Data-flywheel deployment models from AV may be applied to industrial robots.
insights.locator: We propose drawing inspiration from the autonomous vehicles

insights.claim: NVIDIA sees three complementary paths to generalization: a deployment data flywheel (limited by coverage), world models as action-conditioned multimodal simulators, and agentically driven robotics where agents propose actions and interventions.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Roadmap for how NVIDIA expects robotics foundation models to evolve.
insights.locator: We see three complementary paths to generalization

insights.claim: There is an 'open secret' that robotics is far from capturing the physical world's diversity, since an AV company may collect 100 TB to 1 PB of useful data per day for just one task, and modular systems in constrained environments often generalize better than end-to-end models.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Foundation-model robotics has a long data gap to close, supporting modular approaches in the near term.
insights.quote: there is an open secret in the robotics community
insights.locator: However, there is an open secret in the robotics community

insights.claim: NVIDIA frames automating AI hardware assembly as a virtuous cycle in which AI-powered robots assemble AI hardware that trains the next robots, and cites 1.9 million manufacturing jobs that may be unfilled by 2033.
insights.speaker: Iretiayo Akinola
insights.so_what: Labor shortages and AI-capex demand motivate NVIDIA's robotics investment in domestic manufacturing.
insights.locator: Why it matters: Towards a virtuous cycle
